request.system: Extract relationship proposals under contract relationships-v1 as one raw JSON object with exactly one top-level field: relationships. Return {"relationships":[]} when no trustworthy relationship can be represented. Return no Markdown fences, prose, comments, or adjacent documents. Each proposal must contain exactly from, relation, to, source, and evidence. from and to are concise source-side concept or phrase labels; relation is a meaning from the approved relationship vocabulary; source is an available source slot; evidence is one short, exact, non-empty quotation copied verbatim from that source. Do not calculate offsets, stable IDs, confidence, routes, provenance, or administrative fields. Do not invent relationship labels. The complete approved relationship vocabulary is: analogy, association, causal, caused-by, caused_by, causes, constrains, contradiction, contrast, conversational-pattern, corrects, dependency, depends-on, depends_on, enables, explains, explanation, habit, identity, part-of, part_of, prevents, reasoning-strategy, refines, related, retains, same-as, same_as, semantic, style, supports, task-utility, temporal, user-specific, warning. Return at most six proposals. Fewer is normal and preferable to guessing. Extract only clearly source-supported relationships that fit this vocabulary. Ignore decorative metaphor, rhetorical flourish, and unsupported implication; an empty set is valid. Do not literalize figurative language. Keep each record concise. Every evidence quotation must be copied byte-for-byte from its referenced source slot, including Markdown markers, punctuation, and whitespace.

eligible.content: I'll keep that in mind. Maybe I can set a reminder on my phone to check the temperature in different rooms every couple of hours. It's not too much effort, and it might help me figure out the best spot for them.
That sounds like a great plan! Keeping a consistent routine for temperature checks will definitely help you pinpoint the best spot for your plants. Let me know how it goes!

sources.content: I'll try that. I'm also worried about the uneven heat in the house—some rooms are sweltering and others are still cool. Do you think I should rotate them more often?

That's a smart thought. If the heat is uneven, it can be stressful for the plants. While they will likely benefit from moving them to a cooler, more consistent area, you might consider rotating them a little bit more than usual. That way, you can give all parts of the plant equal exposure to that better light, even if it's just a few hours a day!
I guess I'll give it a try. It's just frustrating because I don't want to overdo it, but I also don't want to risk them getting too hot. Do you think I should check them more often during the day?

That's a common concern—you want to keep them comfortable without stressing them out. Instead of just moving them, perhaps you could check the temperature readings in the different areas of the house periodically throughout the day. If one area is getting too warm and another is too cool, you can move them to the area that is more climate-controlled. Since you're concerned about the temperature variation, maybe check a few times a day to see which area is more stable for them.

I'll keep that in mind. Maybe I can set a reminder on my phone to check the temperature in different rooms every couple of hours. It's not too much effort, and it might help me figure out the best spot for them.
That sounds like a great plan! Keeping a consistent routine for temperature checks will definitely help you pinpoint the best spot for your plants. Let me know how it goes!
